issues.description: README example signature change for StorageError.handle is incorrect
issues.detail: The README diff changes `handle(ex, req, resp, params)` to `handle(req, resp, ex, params)`. Falcon's `add_error_handler` expects the signature `(req, resp, ex, params)` for newer versions, but this is a documentation/example change unrelated to the PR's stated purpose (adding POST tests). Mixing unrelated edits into a test-focused PR risks regressions and complicates review.

issues.description: PR scope creep: README and example reformatting unrelated to test additions
issues.detail: The PR title and description focus on adding POST tests and an FAQ entry, but the diff includes large unrelated reformatting of README.rst (line wraps, blank-line removals, %-formatting -> .format, str(status) -> code_to_http_status, stream -> bounded_stream). These should be a separate PR; mixing them obscures the test-related change and hides behavioral shifts like `code_to_http_status`.

issues.description: FAQ example contains a latent bug that contradicts its own purpose
issues.detail: In `PostTest.on_post`, when `Content-Length: 1` is sent with an empty body, `req.stream.read(1)` will block or return b'' depending on the WSGI environment. The example asserts HTTP 400, but relies on the testing harness's behavior — this may not work consistently in production WSGI servers and teaches users a fragile pattern.

issues.description: Description mismatch: claims `req.content_length` was added to `req.stream.read()` but diff shows `bounded_stream`
issues.detail: The PR description says it adds `req.content_length` to `req.stream.read()` in things_advanced.py, but the actual change is `req.stream.read()` -> `req.bounded_stream.read()` with no length argument. The description is misleading reviewers about what the example change actually does, and the rationale for switching to bounded_stream is unexplained.

issues.description: FAQ code example has style issues that will confuse new users
issues.detail: The example uses `assert(result.status == ...)` (parenthesized assert, which is a common pytest anti-pattern—evaluates a tuple if extended), a trailing comma in `[('Content-Length', '1'),]`, and a blank line inside the class. Since this is teaching material, it should model idiomatic style.

issues.description: New tests don't cover the actual bug motivating the example change
issues.detail: The PR references issue #678 and switches to `bounded_stream` in things_advanced.py, but the new tests only exercise normal POST and empty-body-with-Content-Length-1 cases through `simulate_post`. There's no test that would have failed under the old `req.stream.read()` behavior, so the test additions don't actually validate the example fix.

review.summary: This PR conflates a small, useful test addition with a sprawling README reformat and a behavioral change to the things_advanced example (stream -> bounded_stream). The README also includes a signature change to `StorageError.handle` that may or may not match current Falcon error-handler conventions and is unrelated to the stated purpose. The FAQ example teaches a fragile pattern and contains style issues. The new tests don't clearly demonstrate the bug the example change is supposed to fix. Recommend splitting into focused PRs and clarifying the rationale for the bounded_stream switch.
